title: The Same Face, The Same Plate
concept: Two Alaska cities spent the same week arguing about a face and a license plate, from opposite ends of one pipe. Anchorage is buying more capacity to FIND them. Fairbanks bought artificial intelligence to HIDE them so the footage can be released, and it can't keep up. The film holds ONE frame of body-camera video through both cities and asks what the machine actually did to it.

angle.thesis: Fairbanks bought AI to make releasing police video affordable. It made the mechanical half of redaction fast and never touched the half where a person has to decide, so the queue grew anyway. Anchorage is twelve days from funding six hundred thousand dollars more of the capture end of that same pipe. The rule Anchorage did write in 2023 names facial recognition, and the object recognition its plate readers actually run is not the thing that rule named. The protection that held was the one somebody wrote down, and it holds only over the category it named.
supporting_facts: C11/C12/C13: in 2023 the Assembly voted 10 to 1 to HEAVILY LIMIT municipal facial recognition. It is not an indefinite ban, the Assembly may still approve a purchase after a public hearing, and there are carve-outs for human remains, missing persons, trafficking and child-abuse cases. APD does not use it. The film draws this as a rule that WORKS, not as an accusation.
C09: Chief Case said APD does use object recognition FOR ITS LICENSE PLATE READERS. Scope is plate readers only. The film never widens it to the volunteered feeds, the drones or the body cameras.

C14: 'we have no legislative guardrails' is Assembly Member Keith McCormick's CHARACTERIZATION, not an established fact. Anchorage Municipal Code chapter 3.102, Municipal Use of Surveillance Technologies, exists. The film attributes the line to him and draws a category MISMATCH rather than a void.

C22/C23/C24: Fairbanks put AI on redacting police audio and video, has not named the tool, and its chief of staff told the council it is still too slow, while requests went from never above 20 a month before October 2025 to more than 35 in April and more than 35 again in July.

THE MECHANISM, the film's actual AI insight: redaction is two jobs, finding and deciding. AI collapsed finding. Deciding did not move, because a person still signs off on the frame the model missed. So the total barely changed.
angle.fair_counter_point: Drawn at full strength in Act 3, and the fact-check supplied better material for it than the first draft had. ANCHORAGE: Chief Case's strongest argument is de-escalation, in his own words, that better information is 'going to cut down on us coming in too hot'. He volunteers his own limit, 'we are not going to outrun our coverage on this'. Registration is opt-in. City camera footage is discarded after 14 days unless a detective pulls it as evidence. And the Assembly POSTPONED rather than rubber-stamped, which is the check working. FAIRBANKS: Chief Dupee says plainly 'we just don't have the personnel to keep up with the requests. At the end of the day, that's the biggest issue.' The burden lands on ONE evidence technician. State law makes records free under five staff hours a month, a threshold written before body cameras existed. AND THE DECISIVE FAIR BEAT: the chief of staff's 'you'll get it when you get it' was ONE official's idea and the city's own attorneys disagreed with it in the room. The film ends its test there, on the check working, rather than on the official.
angle.valence: mixed, constructive urgency. Not doom, not wry, not celebration. Nothing here has failed: the Assembly postponed rather than rubber-stamped, the 2023 rule is being honored, Fairbanks reported honestly to its own council that its tool did not solve the problem, and the city's own lawyers stopped the bad idea in the room. What earns the urgency is the calendar, because the vote is August 18th.
runners_up: THE SURVEILLANCE FRAME (rejected). All three analysts independently said to cut the Flock exchange, and they were right: APD does not run facial recognition, registration is voluntary, and a dragnet frame is factually wrong and off-brand under config/brand.yaml worldview.

THE FAILED-AI FRAME (rejected). 'Fairbanks bought AI and it didn't work' is the lazy read and it is false. The tool did its job. It was outrun by a demand curve that doubled after it was sized, and it only automated the half of the task that can be automated.

THE PURE-ANCHORAGE FRAME (rejected). The Anchorage vote alone is a governance argument that is fully stated in forty seconds. It can't carry two minutes, and the Fairbanks half is what turns it from a philosophical question into an arithmetic one.

THE HB 377 THREAD (cut on the fact-check's evidence). John McKay's 'most harmful since statehood' quote attaches to the BILL, not to the chief of staff's remark, and splicing them would manufacture a judgment nobody made. The bill also CONTAINED a provision releasing body-camera footage to use-of-force victims within 30 days, so describing it as a transparency rollback would be false. Stating it fairly costs about 40 words the 300-word budget does not have, so the whole thread is cut rather than told badly.

treatment.logline: One frame of police video, a face and a plate inside it, carried through two Alaska cities that spent the same week teaching software to find those two things and paying software to hide them.
treatment.judge_reasoning: The Explainer wins because the payload is a MECHANISM and the mechanism is drawable: one task, two parts, one part collapses and the other does not move. That is a picture, not a paragraph. Grafted from the Dramatist: Act 3 stages the practitioners' case at full strength rather than as a clause, and the evidence technician's month is drawn as a real person's real month. Grafted from the Citizen's Eye: the throughline object and the film's whole thesis image, the same face and the same plate recognized in one city and hidden in the other. Grafted from the Enthusiast: the 2023 rule is drawn as a WIN that held over the category it named, and the film's last honest beat is a city's own attorneys stopping a bad idea in the room, which is what keeps this from reading as a complaint.

retention_plan.the_test: Act 3, 60 to 95 seconds. The fair case gets its own scenes, not a clause. Shot 7 draws the request curve as a real load landing on ONE desk. Shot 8 draws the five-hour rule as a physical measure written for paper and now asked to weigh video. The film says out loud that the chief of staff is right about the problem. It survives because his remedy aims at the requester rather than the bottleneck, and the film proves that with the city's own attorneys disagreeing in the room rather than with an outside critic's adjective.
retention_plan.the_throughline_object: THE FRAME. One frame of body-camera video with a face and a license plate in it. Introduced at 0.0s and visibly different at every act boundary. Its final state is the film's argument.
retention_plan.the_two_loops: PRIMARY plants at 8.5s ('same pipe', stated and refused) and pays at 108.7s when the two cities' frames converge into one. SECONDARY plants at 43.9s (the progress bar appears at zero) and pays at 97.0s (it still has not moved, and that is the answer).
retention_plan.the_padding_test: Applied to every Act 3 beat. Shot 7's request curve and Shot 8's five-hour measure would both have made a 90-second cut WORSE by their absence, because without them the film asserts that Fairbanks has a real constraint instead of showing it, and the counter-point collapses into a token. Two beats that only restated the mechanism more slowly were cut from the script, which is why the VO came in at 300 words rather than 440.

fingerprint.metaphor: the same face and the same plate, found in one city and hidden in the other, out of the same footage

palette: slate #16283C, night #0E1B2A, signal orange #FF6B35 (reserved for machine attention), redaction grey #4A5560, hero light #E8EEF3, shadow #070E17
divergence_note: The last two dispatches were a high-key bone museum interior in cabinet green and brass under overcast-diffuse daylight with a single organic hero and a rise-reveal camera (08-05), and a warm smoke-haze field (08-03). This film inverts every heavy axis of 08-05: pov goes macro-organic to instrument-screen, layout goes grid-modular to hud-instrument-frame, motion goes vertical-descent to radial-emanate, hero goes single-organic-hero to instrument-as-subject, register goes naturalistic-scene to data-brutalist, camera goes rise-reveal to locked-drift, and light goes overcast-diffuse to night-practical. Seven of seven. It is also the first night-interior, screen-lit film this channel has made, and the first with no animal, no landscape and no weather in it at all. DELIBERATE AVOIDANCE, recorded because the near-miss is real: the 2026-07-26 film's thesis image was a WIDE INTAKE and an UNCHANGED NARROW STEM, an asymmetry of volume. This film's mechanism is adjacent and is drawn deliberately differently, as ONE TASK IN TWO SEGMENTS where the mechanical segment collapses and the judgment segment does not move at all. A two-segment bar, never a funnel, never a cranking mouth.

hook.frame1: A single frame of body-camera video, filling the screen, lit only by itself. A face on the left, a license plate on the right, both perfectly sharp. It is the most finished thing this film will draw.
hook.headline: A FACE AND A PLATE
hook.motion_at_frame_1: At 0.4s four orange corner brackets SNAP inward and clamp onto the plate with a hard stop and a tick, in 4 frames with a 1-frame overshoot. It is a real interrupt, not an ease-in: a value slamming to its stop. The face gets no bracket, and the empty air where its bracket should be is the film's whole question.
hook.loopback: The button returns to this exact frame, now with both targets hidden under grey boxes, and pulls back to reveal it is one lit tile in a wall of them.

throughline.object: THE FRAME, one frame of body-camera video carrying a face and a license plate

states.state: RAW. Face and plate both sharp, no brackets, nothing has happened to it yet.
FOUND. The plate is clamped in orange brackets. The face is NOT, and the bracket that starts toward it is refused and slides off, because the 2023 ban holds.
HIDDEN. Two flat grey boxes land on both targets, fast and dead, with no overshoot. A progress bar appears along the bottom edge, at zero.
WAITING. The frame is sitting on a desk in a dark room, boxes on, bar unmoved, one human silhouette behind it and thirty-four more frames stacked beside it.
BOTH AT ONCE. The same frame carries the orange brackets and the grey boxes together, recognized and hidden in one image.
ONE OF MANY. Pulled back until it is a single lit tile in a wall of tiles, with one small person at a desk in front of it.

open_loop.what: Line 1 says two Alaska cities argued about the same two things and calls it 'same pipe', then refuses to show the pipe. The film spends both cities apart and does not put them in one frame until 108.7s, when the orange brackets and the grey boxes land on the SAME frame and the pipe is finally visible as one object.

open_loop_2.what: A progress bar appears along the bottom of the frame the instant the AI starts blurring, and it is at zero. It is never mentioned in the narration. It is visible in four later shots and it never meaningfully moves, and at 97.0s it gets its answer when the remedy on the table turns out to be 'you'll get it when you get it', which is the bar's behaviour stated as policy.

reveals.what: the camera cranes down the face of the wall and it resolves as CAPACITY, a grid of mostly empty dark sockets with a counter climbing against them to its ceiling

the word REDACT splits into a two-segment bar, FIND and DECIDE. The FIND segment collapses to a sliver in 8 frames. The DECIDE segment does not move at all, and the total length barely changes. This is the film's mechanism as a single drawn event.
the Anchorage frame and the Fairbanks frame slide together and FUSE into one frame carrying both the orange brackets and the grey boxes, then the camera begins the pull-back to the wall
the fused frame recedes until it is one tile in a wall where every other tile is bracketed and only this one is hidden, with one small figure beneath it

audio_arc.note: Two real dips. The 74.1 dip is the film's held breath at the technician's desk, where the picture stops moving on purpose. The 113.5 dip is the pre-button silence before the final question, at least 6 dB under the bed.

draw.action: begins collapsing along its length, fast and eased

choreo.reaction: DECIDE holds its exact width

beats.sfx: a hard stop, then nothing at all
beats.means: REVEAL TWO and REHOOK TWO, the film's mechanism
beats.shows: FIND is a sliver, DECIDE has not moved, the total barely changed

draw.subject: the two-segment bar
draw.action: FIND lands as a sliver and DECIDE sits at its original full width, and the total length is almost what it was

choreo.reaction: a measuring rule slides in under the total and confirms it
choreo.ambient: the DECIDE segment's surface is the only textured thing in frame

beats.rehook: the viewer came in thinking this was a story about a tool failing and is shown instead that the tool succeeded completely at a job that was never the bottleneck

beats.sfx: a human pen-scratch, the only organic sound in the film
beats.means: who the judgment half actually is
beats.shows: a hand signs the frame

draw.subject: a hand and the redacted frame
draw.action: signs the corner of the frame, slowly, once

choreo.reaction: the bar advances by one pixel

beats.sfx: a stepping data chatter, one tick per month column
beats.means: the load arrives
beats.shows: the request curve builds

draw.subject: a month-by-month curve
draw.action: builds left to right, flat and low for two years

choreo.reaction: frames begin stacking on the desk below it

beats.sfx: two hard spikes, a beat apart
beats.means: the curve breaks
beats.shows: April and July spike past 35

draw.subject: the curve
draw.action: spikes twice, hard, past the thirty-five line
draw.annotation: APRIL: MORE THAN 35 / JULY: MORE THAN 35

choreo.reaction: the stack of frames doubles in height
choreo.ambient: the bar, still barely off zero

beats.sfx: everything drops out except one hum
beats.means: THE DIP and THROUGHLINE STATE FOUR
beats.shows: one desk, one person, the whole stack

draw.subject: the technician, the stack, the unmoved bar
draw.action: the picture stops. Nothing advances. The person breathes and the stack sits.

choreo.primary: the held breath, a real weight shift above the feet
choreo.reaction: the stack settles by two pixels

beats.sfx: a flat card slap, square and dry, no reverb tail
beats.means: the other side speaks and it is not a straw man. The person being subsidised in that sentence is the evidence technician, and the film draws him standing under it.
beats.shows: the chief of staff's line, plainly set

draw.subject: a quote plate
draw.action: sets down square and stays
draw.annotation: "BASICALLY JUST SUBSIDIZING YOUTUBERS FROM THE LOWER 48"

choreo.reaction: the stack behind it stays exactly as tall

beats.sfx: a brass measure settling
beats.means: the law drawn as a KNOWN OBJECT WITH FIXED CAPACITY rather than as a dial. civics.tsx records that a scale-plate-with-a-needle was drawn three times and dropped, because a dial reports that nothing is measured while a finite spool shows what runs off the end.
beats.shows: the five-hour measure

draw.subject: the five-hour rule as a FullTapeMachine, a finite spool with a FULL tag on a spring
draw.action: settles into frame and its fixed capacity is shown, the reels holding five marked turns
draw.annotation: FREE UNDER 5 STAFF HOURS A MONTH

choreo.primary: the spool settles and its five turns are counted off
choreo.reaction: the FULL tag hangs slack on its spring
choreo.ambient: the tungsten desk practical raking across the reels

beats.sfx: a heavy avalanche settle
beats.means: the throughline object is BACK, and the thing that buries the law is literally the work. v1 vanished the frame for 12.5 seconds at exactly the 80-second how-much-longer mark.
beats.shows: one hour of video buries the scale

draw.subject: a cascade of the same redacted frames, boxes on and bars at zero
draw.action: they pour onto the spool until it seizes, and the needle climbs before it pins

choreo.primary: the tape runs off the end
choreo.reaction: the FULL tag snaps taut

beats.sfx: a paper slap as the slip lands, and the stamp does NOT come down
beats.means: the idea floated at the table, drawn as a slip that is never stamped either way, because that is precisely what it is
beats.shows: the council table, the unstamped slip

draw.subject: the chief of staff and a request slip
draw.action: the slip is set down and NOT stamped, either way
draw.annotation: "YOU'LL GET IT WHEN YOU GET IT"

choreo.reaction: the stamp stays in its cradle

beats.sfx: one clean stroke as the tick is drawn, with a small chime under it
beats.means: THE CONCESSION, drawn on a THING. The problem is real and gets the tick; the remedy is not and does not. v1's subject was 'the diagnosis lifted out as an object', which is the only beat in forty that cannot be drawn.
beats.shows: the diagnosis held up and marked correct

draw.subject: the stack of frames and the one technician from 74.1, brought back
draw.action: a CORRECT tick lands on THEM, while the request slip beside them gets no tick and stays unstamped

choreo.primary: the tick lands on the stack and the technician
choreo.reaction: the slip beside them stays unstamped
choreo.ambient: the tungsten desk practical, the film's judgment colour

beats.sfx: a firm document slide and a low settling tone
beats.means: THE SECOND LOOP PAYS WITH AN EVENT AND A UNIT. v1 paid it by having a rectangle reappear. The film shows exactly one human at a time everywhere else, so making this the only plural frame earns the plural in 'its own attorneys' and escalates in the register the film has been rationing.
beats.shows: the progress bar, still at zero, answered

draw.subject: SEVERAL attorneys at the table, the film's ONLY multi-figure frame, and the hero-white bar returned full width beneath them
draw.action: the slip moves between them and is slid back, and the thirty-five stacked frames lay along the bar to show how little of it one month buys, then it advances exactly ONE pixel

choreo.primary: the slip slides back between several hands
choreo.reaction: the stacked frames lay along the bar and it advances one pixel

beats.rehook: the viewer expects the film to land on the official and instead watches his own city's lawyers stop him, which is the system working and is not what a surveillance story usually does

beats.sfx: a soft, damning click
beats.means: the film's sharpest line, drawn
beats.shows: an unsigned denial

draw.subject: a denial form
draw.action: fills itself in completely except for the signature line, which stays blank

choreo.reaction: the signature line stays conspicuously empty

beats.sfx: a riser starting
beats.means: the film's argument in one line gets the two operations re-fired on the two travelling frames, synced to the two clauses. The convergence becomes the bed under it rather than the whole event.
beats.shows: the two frames slide toward each other

draw.subject: the Anchorage frame and the Fairbanks frame
draw.action: as the first clause lands the orange brackets snap onto the Anchorage frame's plate, and as the second lands the grey boxes drop dead onto the Fairbanks frame, while both travel toward the seam

choreo.reaction: the seam brightens as they close

beats.sfx: a deep sub-bass swell with a soft transient
beats.means: REVEAL THREE and THE PRIMARY LOOP PAYS
beats.shows: one frame carrying brackets and boxes at once

draw.subject: THE FRAME, fused
draw.action: the two become one frame carrying orange brackets AND grey boxes on the same face and the same plate

choreo.reaction: the conduit from 8.5s finally lights along its whole length
choreo.ambient: the wall beginning to resolve behind

beats.sfx: a mechanical date wheel rolling into place with a final detent
beats.means: the one thing a viewer is meant to act on, drawn as a decision that HAS NOT HAPPENED YET rather than as burned text. c3 says postponed, so the film says postponed.
beats.shows: August 18th on the console

draw.subject: a Stamp landing on an EMPTY calendar square, the squares around it already inked
draw.action: the date wheel rolls into place and the stamp seats on the one square that is still blank

choreo.reaction: the fused frame holds

beats.sfx: the bed drops at least 6 dB and the only sound left is the card's flat paper slap
beats.means: the pre-button dip
beats.shows: the stone rule and the paper card, one last time

draw.subject: the seated stone rule and the rocking paper card
draw.action: sit side by side and the card finally falls flat

choreo.reaction: the stone does not move

beats.sfx: the room's air opens up, tile hums layering and multiplying outward
beats.means: THE SIGNATURE SHOT, and it now states the thesis as a picture: hundreds get found, one gets released, by a person. v1 described a big room with a worker in it.
beats.shows: the pull-back to the wall

draw.subject: the fused frame
draw.action: recedes slowly, tiles resolving OUTWARD as the light drains toward one figure. EVERY tile is lit and bracketed in orange. EXACTLY ONE carries a grey box, and the one small figure is seated beneath that single tile.

choreo.primary: the slow recede as tiles resolve outward
choreo.reaction: the tiles immediately behind the figure go dark so the figure stays rim-separated
choreo.ambient: the figure breathing, backlit against lit tiles

beats.sfx: one final tick, then the tail
beats.means: the button
beats.shows: the question over the wall

draw.subject: the closing question
draw.action: types once across the bottom of the wall and holds
draw.annotation: WHAT WOULD YOU WANT WRITTEN DOWN?

choreo.reaction: one tile in the wall flickers
choreo.ambient: the figure still there, still small

beats.sfx: a brass plate seating, then a last low tile hum settling into the tail
beats.means: the branded sign-off and the sources, staged on a real object, and the last frame is still moving
beats.shows: a brass sign-off plate SEATS onto the console lip carrying the wordmark and the sources

draw.subject: a BrassPlate sign-off carrying the wordmark and a sources line
draw.action: SEATS down onto the console lip with real weight and a contact shadow, off the wall and off the figure, while behind it the wall keeps resolving and tiles keep fading up at the frame edges, then a gentle fade
draw.annotation: ALASKA.AI  /  ALASKA'S NEWS SOURCE, KUAC, ALASKA PUBLIC MEDIA, MUNICIPALITY OF ANCHORAGE

choreo.primary: the plate seats onto the console lip with weight
choreo.reaction: its contact shadow lands under it
choreo.ambient: tiles still fading up at the frame edges and the one figure still breathing
